subject: general
question: In the sentence "Scammers masquerade as hiring managers offering attractive jobs," what is the part of speech of the word "masquerade"?
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2** i.e '**Verb**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"masquerade"** in the sentence is a verb.
 
• **Verbs** express actions, occurrences, or states of being. In the sentence, "masquerade" describes the action that the scammers are performing.
 
• The word **"masquerade"** indicates the specific action of pretending or disguising that the scammers are undertaking.
 
• **Verbs** are essential in sentences as they provide the main action or state around which the sentence is structured.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Noun:** A **noun** is a person, place, thing, or idea. "Masquerade" can be a noun in other contexts, but in this sentence, it functions as a verb.
 
• **Adjective:** An **adjective** modifies or describes a noun or pronoun. "Masquerade" does not describe a noun in this sentence.
 
• **Adverb:** An **adverb** modifies a verb, adjective, or other adverb. "Masquerade" is itself a verb and is not modifying another word in this sentence.
